My round-1 claim that it 'would have caught this exact defect' was false. Taking the acceptance's SECOND branch, which the orchestrator named as cheaper and equally honest, and which is the only one I can take without publishing a third form on unrun arithmetic: T-R85 now states that no graded form is known, shows the arithmetic that killed the candidate, and says in as many words 'Do not re-propose it'. As-of-the-band's-own-publication is named as the obvious next candidate and explicitly marked unchecked, together with the reason it is not free: the grader would need a publication instant, and the ledger alone does not carry one. ADR-019 §3's pointer no longer calls T-R85 'the treadmill-free form of the check'; it now states plainly, in bold, that no graded form of 'the published row is the maximum' is currently known, that this class is caught by reading, and that §6's declared slack is the bound that holds meanwhile.
